findings.reason: the section as written would freeze a terminal list blind to a seventh spelling and a text match, so it should state the rule in the owner's terms (not in the live set; the store's own lock predicate) rather than enumerate.
findings.text: s78's first rule makes a job's liveness depend on a closed terminal list (COMPLETED, CANCELLED, FAILED, TIMEOUT, NODE_FAIL, OUT_OF_MEMORY, PREEMPTED), but the codebase already owns that question as the open-ended complement `_JOB_LIVE_STATES = {"running","pending","configuring","completing","suspended"}` with the documented rule "any other readable state means the job has left the queue, which is terminal whatever the scheduler calls it" (`process_liveness.py:49-53`), consumed by `placement_job_alive` (:263-288) and `scheduler_job_state` (:205); a job answered BOOT_FAIL, DEADLINE, REQUEUED or any other terminal spelling outside s78's seven reads unknown and holds the foreign run — the exact defect s78 exists to remove — while the owner's rule already answers it. The same census for s80: `ledger._index_append` (`reckon/ledger.py:3437-3466`) would classify a lock by matching "database is locked" in text, where `run_store._locked` (`reckon/run_store.py:1409-1429`) already answers "did this write lose the lock race", covering both `database is locked` and `database table is locked`, and `run_store._retrying` (reckon/run_store.py:1429) bounds the retry that precedes the refusal — those are the only two classifiers of this kind in the tree (`reckon/crew/station_store.py:363` carries the string for its own store, not for this refusal).

findings.reason: the section must say the placed record keeps answering through its existing `placement`/`job_id` pair and that `launcher_job_id` covers the launch that records none; inverting that grows the pointer for runs that already answer.
findings.text: s78's premise, "a launch records the scheduler job it runs inside … written on the pointer as launcher_job_id beside launcher_host", ignores that a placed dispatch already puts the allocation it runs inside on the pointer as `job_id` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1533-1547`, from the placement hold) and that `placement_job_alive` (`reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:263`, reached from `dispatch_launch._placement_job_alive` at :168-177) already answers the first rule's question — is that job still in the system — for placement-declared schedulers; the launcher's own copy of the same fact is already published on its environment as `FLEET_JOB_ID` (`reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:511`) and in the fleet record's `job_id` (`fleet_supervisor.py:534-545`). As written, the section makes the new field the only source and leaves the placed case's existing evidence unread, so a placed run whose placement answers gets a second, unconsumed record of the same job.

findings.reason: a worker following the text will not add the run-id filter to `read_records`, so the defect the section exists to remove survives its own test.
findings.text: s79 states "`ledger.read_records` already takes the filter `run_store.stored_run_rows` supports, so this narrows the caller rather than adding a reader"; it does not: `read_records` accepts `plan`, `since`, `limit`, `with_figures` and `activity_since` and no run-id selection, while `run_store.stored_run_rows` takes `run_ids` (`reckon/run_store.py:597`, threaded to `_record_rows` at :311-324) and is already called that way at `reckon/crew/open_run_index.py:293` and `:585`. The section asserts reuse that does not exist: passed no filter, `read_records(project, root, plan=slug, with_figures=False)` at `reckon/roadmap.py:1920-1922` keeps decoding every stored row of the plan, and the done-when's "at most 3 rows are decoded" cannot be met.

findings.reason: a third inline vector inside the function that already builds its own queries is brief work; naming an existing format adds nothing the plan needs to state.
findings.text: s78's second rule ("for a record with no launcher job, every job the node lists for this user is either terminal or started after `launched_at`") needs a job start time, which no query vector in the tree selects today: the fleet's own queue read fixes its fields in one format string (`reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:120`, `%i|%j|%T|%M|%R|%b|%k|%L`, used at :338) while `launcher_host_is_gone` writes its query vectors inline in the same function that already calls `process_liveness._run_scheduler_query` (:1458, :1460).
